summary: What US law-firm websites show AI crawlers, measured from the public files and pages of the websites themselves: which of eight named AI crawlers and controls (GPTBot, OAI-SearchBot, ChatGPT-User, ClaudeBot, Claude-User, PerplexityBot, Google-Extended, meta-webindexer) each site's crawler file (the plain-text file at its root that tells crawlers what they may visit) names and whose access to the home page it blocks, whether the apex and www host names lead to one site, how much home-page text a reader gets before JavaScript runs, and how their Spanish pages present themselves. It also counts FAQPage and Organization structured data and nosnippet and max-snippet tags on the same pages. Aggregates by state and market only; no firm or website is named or scored.

records.text: United States: of 44,118 US law-firm websites with a crawler file answer read, 2.2% block the home page for at least one of eight named AI crawlers and controls (GPTBot 2.1%, OAI-SearchBot 0.0%, ClaudeBot 2.0%, PerplexityBot 0.1%, Google-Extended 2.0%); of 44,118 websites, 0.1% show under 200 characters of text before JavaScript runs, 15.6% carry FAQPage markup and 68.2% Organization-family markup; of 42,840 websites, 7.6% have Spanish pages that name no translation service, 0.8% Spanish pages that name one, 3.9% only a translation widget and 87.7% no Spanish pages.
